Passively aggregates system scan results (Beacon / Probe Response) and sends no frames; under system throttling a fresh round arrives roughly every 3-5 seconds.

Bar height = visible AP count; numbers above bars are AP counts, below are the strongest RSSI (dBm). Gold channel numbers 1 / 6 / 11 are the non-overlapping 20 MHz channels.
Tap a bar to expand AP details for that channel.
Scan stopped — start a scan to show 5 GHz channels
No 5 GHz AP found in this scan — no nearby 5G network or the device does not support 5 GHz
Lists only the common 5 GHz channels seen in this scan; channel number = 5000 + 5 × N MHz. Tap a row to view AP details for that channel.
All values come from real WifiManager.scanResults snapshots — no interpolation, simulation or smoothing; missing data shows \"--\".
Only APs actively broadcasting Beacons are visible: hidden-SSID APs never appear in scanResults and are not counted.
Channel occupancy = visible AP count, not live spectrum or airtime utilization; a channel with few but busy APs can still be congested.
Scans are throttled by the system to roughly one round every 3-5 seconds; table values are the latest snapshot, not live spectrum.
RSSI is the received strength at the phone antenna (dBm); distance, walls and orientation affect it — it does not represent AP transmit power.
Android 9+ requires system location enabled and precise location permission granted, otherwise scan results stay empty.
Security type follows Beacon capabilities: WPA2/WPA3 mixed mode counts as WPA3; 6 GHz and uncommon channels are not counted.
